name: Basic Mechanical Engineering Lab
objectives: To help students visualize various concepts and perform experiments on different apparatus to gain practical knowledge in basic mechanical engineering.
outcomes: Understand and explain the functioning of SI and CI engines.
Understand the internal operation occurring in the working of fluid machines.
Perform the impact test (Izod/Charpy) on the impact testing machine.
Understand concepts like moment of inertia and coefficient of friction by performing on the apparatus.
Perform and study various measurement instruments.
rule: A minimum of 10 experiments from the following
note:
Record format: aim, apparatus and specifications, neat labelled sketch, theory with formulas, observation table with units, sample calculation, graph if required, result and precautions.
For testing machines (UTM, impact) record the specimen dimensions before the test and the load or energy readings; draw the load-extension curve with the yield, ultimate and fracture points marked.
In viva, be ready to name the parts of the model or machine, state the working principle in two lines and say the sources of error.

exps.title: Study of 2-stroke and 4-stroke I.C. engine models
exps.aim: Understand the parts and working cycle of two-stroke and four-stroke engines.
exps.apparatus: Cut-section models of 2-stroke and 4-stroke petrol engines
exps.formula: 4-stroke: one power stroke every 2 revolutions (720°); 2-stroke: one every revolution. Otto efficiency η = 1 − 1/r^{γ−1}.
viva: Name the four strokes of a four-stroke engine.
Suction (intake), compression, power (expansion) and exhaust.
How many crankshaft revolutions per cycle in a 2-stroke and a 4-stroke engine?
One for a two-stroke and two for a four-stroke.
What are the ports in a 2-stroke engine used for?
Inlet, transfer and exhaust ports replace valves and control the gas flow.

exps.title: Study of Fiat engine and/or diesel engine prototype
exps.aim: Study the construction, parts and working of a petrol (Fiat) or diesel engine prototype.
exps.apparatus: Fiat engine or diesel engine prototype, models of piston, valve, crankshaft, fuel injector
exps.formula: Compression ratio r = (V_s + V_c)/V_c; SI engine r ≈ 6-10, CI engine r ≈ 14-22.
viva: How does a CI engine ignite the fuel?
Compression heats the air above the fuel's ignition temperature, so injected fuel ignites by itself.
Why does a diesel engine have a higher compression ratio?
Compression alone must ignite the fuel, so it needs higher air temperature.
Name the main parts of an engine.
Cylinder, piston, connecting rod, crankshaft, valves, camshaft and flywheel.

exps.title: To conduct the tensile test on a UTM and determine ultimate tensile strength and percentage elongation for a steel specimen
exps.aim: Pull a steel specimen to failure and obtain its stress-strain behaviour and key strength values.
exps.apparatus: Universal testing machine, steel specimen, vernier caliper, extensometer, marking punch
exps.formula: UTS = P_max/A₀; % elongation = (L_f − L₀)/L₀ × 100; % reduction in area = (A₀ − A_f)/A₀ × 100; E = σ/ε in the elastic range.
viva: What is the yield point?
The stress at which the material begins to deform plastically without a load increase.
What is ductility and how is it measured?
Ability to deform plastically before fracture; measured by percentage elongation and reduction in area.
Why is gauge length marked on the specimen?
Elongation is measured over a fixed gauge length, so the results are comparable.

exps.title: To conduct the compression test and determine the ultimate compressive strength for a specimen
exps.aim: Load a specimen in compression until failure and calculate its compressive strength.
exps.apparatus: UTM or compression testing machine, cast iron or concrete specimen, vernier caliper
exps.formula: σ_c = P_max/A₀; brittle materials such as cast iron fail by shear near 45°.
viva: Which materials are strong in compression?
Brittle materials such as cast iron and concrete are much stronger in compression than in tension.
How does cast iron fail in compression?
By shear along a plane inclined at roughly 45° to the axis.
Why is a specimen with a small L/D ratio used?
To avoid buckling, so that failure is by crushing.

exps.title: To conduct the impact test (Izod/Charpy) on the impact testing machine and to find the impact strength
exps.aim: Find the energy absorbed by a notched specimen when struck by a swinging pendulum.
exps.apparatus: Impact testing machine (Izod or Charpy), notched specimens, vernier caliper
exps.formula: Energy absorbed = mg R(cosβ − cosα) (J); impact strength = energy/cross-section area at the notch.
viva: Difference between Izod and Charpy tests?
Charpy uses a simply supported beam struck at the middle; Izod uses a cantilever struck at the free end.
Why is the specimen notched?
The notch concentrates stress and triggers the fracture under worst-case conditions.
What does high impact strength show?
High toughness, meaning the material absorbs a lot of energy before fracture.

exps.title: To determine the value of acceleration due to gravity by Atwood's machine apparatus
exps.aim: Measure the acceleration of two unequal masses over a pulley and calculate g.
exps.apparatus: Atwood machine, pulley, thread, two masses, stop-watch, scale
exps.formula: a = (m₁ − m₂)g/(m₁ + m₂); a = 2s/t², so g = 2s(m₁ + m₂)/[t²(m₁ − m₂)]. Tension T = 2m₁m₂g/(m₁ + m₂).
viva: Why is the difference in masses small?
A small difference gives a small acceleration that can be timed accurately.
What is neglected in the formula?
Mass of the string, pulley inertia and friction.
What is the tension in the string?
T = 2m₁m₂g/(m₁ + m₂).

exps.title: To verify the principle of moments by bell crank lever apparatus
exps.aim: Verify that the sum of clockwise and anticlockwise moments about the fulcrum is equal at equilibrium.
exps.apparatus: Bell crank lever apparatus, weights, hanger, scale
exps.formula: W·a = P·b (moments about the fulcrum); clockwise moments = anticlockwise moments.
viva: State the principle of moments.
For a body in equilibrium the sum of clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments.
What is a bell crank lever used for?
To change the direction of a force by 90° and amplify it.
Where is the fulcrum located?
At the junction of the two arms, which are set at right angles.

exps.title: To determine the moment of inertia of a flywheel apparatus about its axis of rotation
exps.aim: Find the moment of inertia of a flywheel by letting a falling mass rotate it.
exps.apparatus: Flywheel with axle, hanging mass, string, stop-watch, vernier caliper, scale
exps.formula: I = m r²(g t²/(2h) − 1), neglecting friction; r = axle radius, h = fall height, t = time of fall.
viva: What is moment of inertia?
The rotational analogue of mass: I = Σmr², resistance to change in angular motion.
Why does a flywheel have most of its mass at the rim?
A large I at the rim smooths out speed fluctuations.
What is the SI unit of I?
kg·m².

exps.title: To verify Newton's second law of motion by Fletcher's trolley apparatus
exps.aim: Show that acceleration is proportional to force when mass is constant, and inversely proportional to mass at constant force.
exps.apparatus: Fletcher's trolley, inclined or horizontal track, weights, pulley, stop-watch, scale
exps.formula: F = ma; a = 2s/t². Plot a against F, a straight line through the origin.
viva: State Newton's second law.
The rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force, so F = ma for constant mass.
Why is friction compensated on the track?
Otherwise the measured net force would be less than the applied force.
What does the a-F graph show?
A straight line whose slope is 1/m.

exps.title: To find the coefficient of friction by combined inclined plane and friction slide apparatus
exps.aim: Determine the coefficient of friction between two surfaces using an inclined plane and a slide.
exps.apparatus: Inclined plane with friction slide, blocks, weights, protractor, pulley
exps.formula: μ = tanφ (angle of friction, equal to angle of repose); on horizontal slide μ = F/N.
viva: Define the coefficient of friction.
The ratio of limiting friction to the normal reaction, μ = F/N.
What is the angle of repose?
The maximum slope at which a body stays at rest without sliding; tanφ = μ.
Is static or kinetic friction greater?
Static (limiting) friction is greater than kinetic friction.

exps.title: To verify Bernoulli's equation
exps.aim: Verify the conservation of energy of a flowing fluid using a Venturimeter or a tapered pipe.
exps.apparatus: Bernoulli's apparatus, Venturi tube with piezometers, water supply, measuring tank, stop-watch
exps.formula: p/ρg + v²/2g + z = constant (total head); v = Q/A.
viva: State Bernoulli's theorem.
For steady, incompressible, non-viscous flow, the total energy per unit weight along a streamline stays constant.
What is the significance of pressure head, velocity head and datum head?
They are the energy per unit weight due to pressure, motion and elevation.
Why do the measured heads differ slightly from ideal?
Viscous losses cause a small drop in total head.

exps.title: Study and working of hydraulic turbines and pumps
exps.aim: Understand the construction and working of Pelton, Francis, Kaplan turbines and centrifugal and reciprocating pumps.
exps.apparatus: Models of Pelton wheel, Francis turbine, Kaplan turbine, centrifugal pump, reciprocating pump
exps.formula: Pelton: impulse, high head. Francis: reaction, medium head. Kaplan: axial flow, low head. Specific speed N_s = N√P/H^{5/4}.
viva: Which turbine suits high head and low discharge?
Pelton wheel, an impulse turbine.
What is priming of a centrifugal pump?
Filling the casing and suction pipe with liquid before start so that air does not stop pumping.
What is the difference between impulse and reaction turbines?
In impulse, the water pressure is atmospheric at the runner; in reaction, pressure drops across the runner.

exps.title: Study and working of different types of measuring instruments like vernier caliper, micrometer, height gauge, sine bar, dial gauge etc.
exps.aim: Learn the principle, least count and use of common linear and angular measuring instruments.
exps.apparatus: Vernier caliper, outside micrometer, height gauge, sine bar with slip gauges, dial gauge, surface plate
exps.formula: Vernier least count = 1 MSD − 1 VSD (e.g. 0.02 mm); micrometer LC = pitch/divisions = 0.5/50 = 0.01 mm; sine bar: sinθ = h/L.
viva: What is least count?
The smallest length an instrument can measure accurately.
What is zero error?
A non-zero reading when the jaws are closed; it is subtracted from the readings.
How does a sine bar measure angles?
With slip gauges of height h under one roller, sinθ = h/L, L being the roller spacing.

exps.title: Identification of twenty five common materials and their application
exps.aim: Recognise common engineering materials and state their properties and uses.
exps.apparatus: Sample set of metals, alloys, polymers, ceramics and composites
exps.formula: Classes: ferrous (mild steel, cast iron), non-ferrous (Al, Cu, brass = Cu + Zn, bronze = Cu + Sn), polymers, ceramics and composites.
viva: What is the difference between brass and bronze?
Brass is a copper-zinc alloy; bronze is a copper-tin alloy.
What is the carbon content of mild steel and cast iron?
Mild steel has about 0.15-0.3 % C; cast iron has about 2-4 % C.
Why is aluminium used in aircraft?
Its high strength-to-weight ratio and corrosion resistance.
